title: Karel Čapek's birth chart
metaDescription: Karel Čapek's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 19.2° Capricorn. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: 0.6° separates the Sun and Jupiter from an exact conjunction; at that range identity and expansion read as one mechanism. When two functions occupy one degree, the tradition reads a fusion: neither can act without committing the other.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's position resolves to 19.2° Capricorn — deep enough in the second decan (10°–20°) that Venus, its traditional sub-ruler, colours the reading.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 7.1° Aquarius; Venus stands at 9.6° Capricorn; Mars stands at 4.7° Scorpio. The tradition reads thought that travels by comparison from Mercury, attraction that grows by reliability from Venus, effort that surges when it matters from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins the Sun and Jupiter — a conjunction holding at 0.6°. When two functions occupy one degree, the tradition reads a fusion: neither can act without committing the other. Behind it, Saturn square Neptune at 1.3°, and Mars sextile Saturn at 1.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Every angle named here holds for the whole of that day at the birthplace, so an unknown hour cannot take it away.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks two placements here. Mars in Scorpio at 4.7° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Capricorn at 19.8° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given. The table describes circumstance rather than quality — a planet in detriment is inconvenienced, not diminished.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Balance, counted honestly across the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: elements earth 4, air 4, water 1; modalities cardinal 4, mutable 3, fixed 2. Earth counts what remains: the built, the kept, the finished. Promise weighs less than delivery. No settled placement falls in fire — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Saturn, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Leo into Virgo during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.0° between one midnight and the next. Half the day belongs to each sign, and the split falls at an unrecorded hour — so this page holds the Moon as a genuine unknown.
